rv.q: Sunny Afternoon is a hymn to English musical individualism and artistic perseverance - all with the miniskirts and freshness of 1960s London.
And still it works fantastically well.
When a number is given the full treatment by the top-notch quartet of actor-musicians who make up the band, it's an utterly joyous sound.
This is the best musical I have ever seen!
If all jukebox musicals were as well crafted as Sunny Afternoon , the genre would have a much better reputation than it does.
The show is nippy, colourful and euphoric.
Unlike the songs, originally written full of clever observations and performed with high octane energy, the whole musical was bland and flat.
Sunny Afternoon is a triumphant celebration of The Kinks’ music.
I'm sure it's authentic, but I'm not sure it provides enough drama to sustain a show that clocks in at three hours.

cn.t: Critics praise this well-crafted Kinks musical for its strong performances and excellent use of the band's catalogue, though some find the biographical narrative relentlessly downbeat compared to similar jukebox musicals.
